Also called etiology, causative factor, underlying reason. Examples: "HIV virus" as a cause of AIDS, "pulmonary embolism" as a cause of cardiac arrest, "bacterial infection".

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

types.embedding_query_text: Disease: A disorder of structure or function in a human, animal, or plant, especially one that produces specific signs or symptoms or that affects a specific location and is not simply a direct result of physical injury. Also called illness, sickness, ailment, malady. Examples: Covid-19 infection, respiratory diseases, Covid.

chosen_type.label: MedicalCondition
chosen_type.justification: MedicalCondition is a broader category that encompasses all diseases, including both infectious and non-infectious ones mentioned.

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: DDxElement
candidates.comment: A DDxElement is an alternative, closely-related medical condition considered during differential diagnosis, along with the distinguishing signs. Also called differential diagnosis item, alternative diagnosis, rule-out condition. Examples: Considering "strep throat" as a DDxElement for a patient presenting with a sore throat and fever, alongside "common cold."

types.embedding_query_text: OrganizationType: A classification or category of organizations based on their nature, purpose, or structure. Also called organizational category, type of institution. Examples: medical societies.

chosen_type.label: BusinessEntityType
chosen_type.justification: 'Medical societies' describes a classification of organizations, which aligns with schema.org/BusinessEntityType.

candidates.label: NonprofitType
candidates.comment: NonprofitType is an enumeration for various official non-profit organization types. Also called charity type, non-profit classification. Examples: 501(c)(3) (US), Registered Charity (UK), Gemeinnütziger Verein (Germany). Distinct from NLNonprofitType, which is specific to the Netherlands.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: BusinessEntityType
candidates.comment: A BusinessEntityType is an Enumeration representing the legal form, size, main line of business, or position in the value chain of an organization or business person. Also called legal entity type, company structure, business classification. Examples: Corporation, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Non-profit Organization.

candidates.label: USNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.

types.embedding_query_text: Document: A piece of written, printed, or electronic matter that provides information or evidence or that serves as an official record. Also called record, report, text, publication. Examples: guidelines, news release, correction, Recommendations.

chosen_type.label: Report
chosen_type.justification: Mentions like 'guidelines', 'news release', and 'Recommendations' are all types of reports or official documents.

candidates.label: NoteDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A NoteDigitalDocument, as a DigitalDocument, is a file containing a note, primarily for the author's reference. Also called digital note, electronic memo, text note. Examples: a personal reminder in a digital format, a draft of an idea, a quick thought saved electronically. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is intended for public consumption.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: Report
candidates.comment: A Report is an Article generated by a governmental or non-governmental organization. Also called official report, document, publication. Examples: an annual financial report, a government research report, a UN policy report, a company's sustainability report.

candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

candidates.label: Manuscript
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.

types.embedding_query_text: DocumentCollection: A compilation or archive of various documents. Also called archive, collection of texts, body of work. Examples: literature.

chosen_type.label: Collection
chosen_type.justification: 'Literature' refers to a body of written works, which is a type of collection.

candidates.label: ProductCollection
candidates.comment: A ProductCollection is a Collection of products, either ProductGroups or specific variants, listed together, often within an Offer. Also called product assortment, product bundle, product set. Examples: a collection of books by an author, a bundle of software products, a set of kitchen utensils, a curated selection of wines.

candidates.label: Collection
candidates.comment: A grouping of various items, which can include creative works or products. Also called assortment, compilation, set, aggregate. Examples: A collection of rare books, a stamp collection, a music album, a product catalog.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

candidates.label: MediaGallery
candidates.comment: A web page that serves as a collection page for various media, such as images, videos, and other multimedia. Also called multimedia gallery, photo and video collection, digital media showcase. Examples: a website's image gallery, a video portfolio page, a mixed-media art exhibition page.

candidates.label: ArchiveComponent
candidates.comment: An ArchiveComponent is an intangible CreativeWork representing any content within an archive, whether an individual item or a collection, described by specific archival properties. Also called archival item, archival record, archive content, collection item. Examples: a historical letter, a collection of photographs, a government document series, a digital archive file.

types.embedding_query_text: ResearchStudy: A systematic investigation, including research development, testing, and evaluation, designed to develop or contribute to generalizable knowledge. Also called study, research project, investigation, experiment. Examples: study.

chosen_type.label: MedicalStudy
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type and mention directly match the definition of schema.org/MedicalStudy.

candidates.label: MedicalStudy
candidates.comment: A medical entity that is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health. Also called clinical study, health research, medical investigation. Examples: a drug trial, an epidemiological survey, a patient registry. Distinct from MedicalScholarlyArticle, which is the publication of study results, not the study itself.

candidates.label: MedicalObservationalStudy
candidates.comment: A medical study that infers the effect of a treatment by observing a cohort of subjects over time, without investigator control over treatment assignment. Also called observational research, cohort study, epidemiological study. Examples: a study tracking health outcomes in smokers vs. non-smokers, a study on diet and disease incidence. Distinct from MedicalTrial, where subjects are randomly assigned to treatment groups.

candidates.label: MedicalTrial
candidates.comment: A medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or procedures, typically with random allocation to groups. Also called clinical trial, randomized controlled trial, interventional study. Examples: a Phase 3 drug trial, a study comparing two surgical techniques, a vaccine efficacy trial. Distinct from MedicalObservationalStudy, where treatment assignment is not controlled by the investigator.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: MedicalStudyStatus
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing the status of a medical study. Also called study phase, research status, trial stage. Examples: "Recruiting", "Active, not recruiting", "Completed", "Terminated".

types.embedding_query_text: Information: Facts provided or learned about something or someone. Also called data, knowledge, intelligence, facts. Examples: data, information.

chosen_type.label: Information
chosen_type.definition: Facts provided or learned about something or someone.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type broadly represents the abstract concept of 'Information'; Intangible is a suitable parent.

candidates.label: DataFeedItem
candidates.comment: A DataFeedItem is an individual entry or record contained within a larger DataFeed. Also called feed entry, feed item, data record. Examples: A single news article in an RSS feed, one product listing in an inventory feed, a single weather observation in a data stream.

candidates.label: DataFeed
candidates.comment: A DataFeed is a continuous stream or single file of structured information, typically updated regularly, about one or more entities or topics. Also called RSS feed, Atom feed, data stream, information feed. Examples: A news RSS feed, a stock market data feed, a product inventory feed, a weather data API.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: NutritionInformation
candidates.comment: NutritionInformation, as a StructuredValue, provides details about the nutritional content of food, often for a recipe. Also called nutritional facts, food label information, dietary data. Examples: calorie count, fat content, protein amount, vitamin percentages. Distinct from Recipe, which describes how to prepare food.

types.embedding_query_text: Communication: The imparting or exchanging of information by speaking, writing, or using some other medium. Also called message, correspondence, dialogue, transmission. Examples: text messages, exchange.

chosen_type.label: Conversation
chosen_type.justification: 'Text messages' and 'exchange' imply a series of communications, which fits the definition of schema.org/Conversation.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: CommunicateAction
candidates.comment: The act of transmitting information to another person or entity through a specific medium. Also called communication, conveying information, interacting. Examples: Sending an email, making a phone call, giving a speech, writing a letter. Distinct from InteractAction, which is a broader category of actions involving interaction.

candidates.label: Message
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a single communication from a sender to one or more recipients. Also called communication, dispatch, note, email. Examples: an email, a text message, a direct message on social media, a voicemail.

candidates.label: ReplyAction
candidates.comment: ReplyAction is a CommunicateAction representing the act of responding to a question or message. Also called answering, responding, writing back. Examples: replying to an email, answering a question on a forum, responding to a text message, commenting on a social media post. Distinct from AskAction, which is the origin of a reply.

candidates.label: EmailMessage
candidates.comment: An EmailMessage is a CreativeWork representing a message sent via electronic mail. Also called email, electronic mail, e-message. Examples: A business correspondence email, a personal email to a friend, a newsletter subscription email, a spam message.

types.embedding_query_text: Device: A thing made or adapted for a particular purpose, especially a piece of mechanical or electronic equipment. Also called gadget, apparatus, instrument, tool. Examples: Dr. Anthony Fauci’s former government phone.

chosen_type.label: Product
chosen_type.justification: A 'phone' is a manufactured good, which is a type of product.

mentions: Dr. Anthony Fauci’s former government phone

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: MedicalDevice
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any object used in a medical capacity for diagnosing or treating a patient. Also called medical instrument, healthcare apparatus, diagnostic tool. Examples: a stethoscope, an MRI machine, a surgical scalpel, a blood pressure monitor.

candidates.label: MedicalDevicePurpose
candidates.comment: An enumeration of categories for medical devices, organized by their purpose or intended use. Also called device use, medical equipment function, intended purpose. Examples: "Diagnostic", "Therapeutic", "Surgical", "Monitoring".

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: MotorizedBicycle
candidates.comment: A vehicle that is primarily a bicycle equipped with an attached motor for power or assistance. Also called e-bike, electric bicycle, moped (older sense). Examples: a pedal-assist electric bicycle, a bicycle with a small gas engine kit. Distinct from Motorcycle, which is designed from the ground up as a motor vehicle.

types.embedding_query_text: Process: A series of actions or steps taken in order to achieve a particular end. Also called procedure, method, operation, course of action. Examples: investigation.

chosen_type.label: Process
chosen_type.definition: A series of actions or steps taken in order to achieve a particular end.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a general 'Process' or 'investigation'; Action is a suitable parent as a process is a series of actions.

candidates.label: DiscoverAction
candidates.comment: A find action representing the act of finding or uncovering an object or information. Also called Find, uncover, locate, detect, unearth. Examples: Discovering a new species, finding a lost item, uncovering a historical artifact, detecting a bug in software. Distinct from FindAction, which is a broader category for seeking something.

candidates.label: SearchAction
candidates.comment: The act of looking for an object or information, often using a search engine or database. Also called searching, querying, looking up, seeking. Examples: typing a query into Google, searching for a file on a computer, looking up a contact in a directory. Distinct from FindAction, which is the result of a search, not the act itself.

candidates.label: CheckAction
candidates.comment: The act of an agent inspecting, investigating, or examining an object's accuracy, quality, or condition. Also called verify, inspect, examine, audit, review. Examples: Checking a document for errors, checking a car's oil level, checking a patient's vital signs.

candidates.label: FindAction
candidates.comment: FindAction is an Action representing the act of locating an object. Also called discover, locate, unearth. Examples: Finding a lost key, discovering a new species, locating a specific document, unearthing an artifact. Distinct from SearchAction, which is generally a precursor to FindAction.

candidates.label: CreateAction
candidates.comment: A CreateAction is the act of deliberately producing, generating, or building a new result or entity by an agent. Also called production, generation, fabrication, construction. Examples: Writing a book, composing a song, building a house, designing a website.

types.embedding_query_text: RoleAndActions: The specific function or part played by someone, along with the activities they perform. Also called responsibilities, duties, conduct, performance. Examples: health official’s leadership and actions.

chosen_type.label: OrganizationRole
chosen_type.justification: 'Health official’s leadership' describes a specific function within an organization, which aligns with schema.org/OrganizationRole.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: LoginAction
candidates.comment: The action of gaining access to a device or application by providing credentials. Also called sign in, log on, user authentication. Examples: logging into a website, signing into a mobile app, logging onto a computer. Distinct from ControlAction, which is a broader category for actions that control something.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

types.embedding_query_text: Opinion: A view or judgment formed about something, not necessarily based on fact or knowledge. Also called viewpoint, belief, stance, perspective. Examples: criticism.

chosen_type.label: Comment
chosen_type.justification: 'Criticism' is a form of remark or observation, which can be represented as a schema.org/Comment.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

candidates.label: Comment
candidates.comment: A textual remark or observation made about an item, such as a blog post. Also called remark, feedback, note, annotation. Examples: A user's comment on a YouTube video, a review on a product page, a blog post comment, a code comment.

candidates.label: UserReview
candidates.comment: A review or critique created by an end-user, such as a consumer or attendee, rather than a professional critic. Also called customer review, consumer feedback, public review. Examples: a customer's product review on an e-commerce site, a diner's restaurant review, an audience member's movie review. Distinct from CriticReview, which is a review written by a professional critic.

candidates.label: OpinionNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An OpinionNewsArticle, as a NewsArticle, primarily expresses opinions rather than journalistic reporting of news and events. Also called opinion piece, editorial, column. Examples: an editorial in a newspaper, a political commentary, a personal essay in the opinion section. Distinct from Report, which presents factual findings.

candidates.label: AssessAction
candidates.comment: An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate. Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.

types.embedding_query_text: MathematicalConcept: An abstract idea or principle in mathematics. Also called mathematical idea, abstract concept. Examples: denominator.

chosen_type.label: MathematicalConcept
chosen_type.definition: An abstract idea or principle in mathematics.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type represents a general mathematical concept like 'denominator'; Intangible is a suitable parent.

candidates.label: SolveMathAction
candidates.comment: The action of taking a mathematical expression and directing users to a resource capable of solving or simplifying it. Also called math solving, equation solving, calculation action. Examples: entering '2+2' into a calculator app, inputting a complex equation into Wolfram Alpha, using a math solver website.

candidates.label: MathSolver
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a tool or application capable of solving a subset of mathematical problems. Also called mathematical calculator, problem solver, equation solver. Examples: an online algebra solver, a geometry calculator, a calculus problem-solving app.

candidates.label: DefinedTermSet
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a collection of formally defined terms, such as a glossary, dictionary, or classification scheme. Also called Glossary, vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, enumeration. Examples: The Dewey Decimal Classification system, a medical dictionary, a list of product categories, a set of industry standards. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a single entry within such a set.

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

types.embedding_query_text: SampleGroup: A subset of a population selected for a study or experiment. Also called sample, study group, cohort. Examples: full sample of nearly 4,000 participants.

chosen_type.label: StatisticalPopulation
chosen_type.justification: A sample group is a subset of a population used for statistical analysis, fitting the definition of schema.org/StatisticalPopulation.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: MedicalObservationalStudy
candidates.comment: A medical study that infers the effect of a treatment by observing a cohort of subjects over time, without investigator control over treatment assignment. Also called observational research, cohort study, epidemiological study. Examples: a study tracking health outcomes in smokers vs. non-smokers, a study on diet and disease incidence. Distinct from MedicalTrial, where subjects are randomly assigned to treatment groups.

candidates.label: DanceGroup
candidates.comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

types.embedding_query_text: Calculation: A mathematical determination of the size or number of something. Also called computation, estimation, figure. Examples: risk estimate.

chosen_type.label: Calculation
chosen_type.definition: A mathematical determination of the size or number of something.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type represents the result of a calculation or estimate; QuantitativeValue is a suitable parent for a numerical result.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskCalculator
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a complex mathematical calculation, often requiring an online tool, used to assess prognosis. Also called prognosis calculator, risk assessment tool, clinical prediction model. Examples: a calculator for cardiovascular disease risk, a tool for predicting cancer recurrence. Distinct from MedicalRiskScore, which is a simpler sum of risk factors.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: SolveMathAction
candidates.comment: The action of taking a mathematical expression and directing users to a resource capable of solving or simplifying it. Also called math solving, equation solving, calculation action. Examples: entering '2+2' into a calculator app, inputting a complex equation into Wolfram Alpha, using a math solver website.

candidates.label: Float
candidates.comment: Float is a Number data type representing a floating-point number. Also called decimal number, real number. Examples: 3.14, -0.5, 100.0, 2.718.

candidates.label: Integer
candidates.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

types.embedding_query_text: PositiveOutcome: A favorable or desirable result or consequence. Also called advantage, gain, positive result, good effect. Examples: benefits.

chosen_type.label: PositiveOutcome
chosen_type.definition: A favorable or desirable result or consequence.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a general 'Positive Outcome' or 'benefit'; Intangible is a suitable parent for an abstract concept.

candidates.label: WinAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: OfferForLease
candidates.comment: An OfferForLease, as an Offer, represents a proposal to lease out something. Also called lease offer, rental offer, tenancy proposal. Examples: an offer to lease an apartment, a car lease deal, equipment rental terms. Distinct from OfferForPurchase, which is an offer to sell.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: EndorsementRating
candidates.comment: An EndorsementRating is a Rating that expresses a positive level of endorsement, such as a "critic's pick" or a social media "Like," often without a numeric scale. Also called positive rating, approval rating, recommendation. Examples: A "thumbs up" icon, a "recommended by critics" badge, a social media "Like" count, inclusion in a "best of" list.

types.embedding_query_text: NegativeOutcome: An unfavorable or undesirable result or consequence. Also called disadvantage, detriment, adverse effect, harm. Examples: risks.

chosen_type.label: NegativeOutcome
chosen_type.definition: An undesirable or unfavorable result or consequence.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a general 'Negative Outcome' or 'risk'; Intangible is a suitable parent for an abstract concept.

candidates.label: DislikeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative sentiment or disapproval towards an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express dislike, disapprove of, show aversion, downvote. Examples: Disliking a movie, expressing disapproval of a policy, downvoting a comment online. Distinct from LikeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or approval.

candidates.label: LoseAction
candidates.comment: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity or contest. Also called suffer defeat, be beaten, fail to win. Examples: losing a game, being defeated in an election, failing a competition. Distinct from AchieveAction, which is a broader category for actions that result in an outcome.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

candidates.label: UnRegisterAction
candidates.comment: The act of formally removing oneself from a service, membership, or registration. Also called unsubscribe, deregister, cancel registration. Examples: unregistering from a website, unsubscribing from a newsletter, canceling a gym membership. Distinct from LeaveAction, which implies departing a group or team rather than a service.

candidates.label: CancelAction
candidates.comment: The act of asserting that a future event or action will no longer occur. Also called call off, revoke, annul, abort. Examples: Cancelling a flight, cancelling a meeting, cancelling a subscription. Distinct from ConfirmAction, which is asserting an event will happen.

types.embedding_query_text: MedicalProfessionalGroup Examples: doctors.

chosen_type.label: MedicalProfessionalGroup
chosen_type.definition: A group of individuals who work in the healthcare field and provide medical services.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type specifically represents a group of medical professionals; MedicalOrganization is the closest parent.

candidates.label: Physician
candidates.comment: A Physician, as a MedicalBusiness, is an individual doctor or a doctor's office considered as a MedicalOrganization. Also called doctor, medical practitioner, medical doctor. Examples: a general practitioner, a specialist physician, a family doctor's clinic. Distinct from Hospital, which is a larger medical facility.

candidates.label: PhysiciansOffice
candidates.comment: A PhysiciansOffice, as a Physician, is a doctor's office or clinic where medical consultations and treatments are provided. Also called doctor's clinic, medical office, medical practice. Examples: a family doctor's practice, a specialist's clinic, an urgent care center. Distinct from Hospital, which offers inpatient care and emergency services.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: HealthPlanNetwork
candidates.comment: A HealthPlanNetwork is an intangible collection of healthcare providers, such as doctors and hospitals, that contract with a health insurance plan to provide services at negotiated rates. Also called provider network, insurance network, healthcare provider group. Examples: an HMO network, a PPO network, a specific hospital system affiliated with an insurer.

candidates.label: MedicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a process of care, invasive or non-invasive, used for diagnostic, therapeutic, preventive, or palliative purposes. Also called medical intervention, clinical procedure, healthcare process. Examples: "surgery", "biopsy", "vaccination", "physical therapy".

types.embedding_query_text: MedicalProcedure: A course of action intended to achieve a result in medical care. Also called treatment, medical act, clinical intervention. Examples: intervention.

chosen_type.label: MedicalProcedure
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type and mention 'intervention' directly match the general definition of schema.org/MedicalProcedure.

candidates.label: TherapeuticProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure specifically intended to treat a health condition or improve a patient's well-being. Also called medical treatment, therapy, healing procedure. Examples: chemotherapy, physical therapy, surgical removal of a tumor.

candidates.label: SurgicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure involving an incision with instruments, performed for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. Also called surgery, operation, medical incision, surgical intervention. Examples: an appendectomy, a knee replacement surgery, a biopsy, a C-section.

candidates.label: MedicalTherapy
candidates.comment: A therapeutic medical procedure designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions. Also called medical treatment, healthcare intervention, therapy regimen. Examples: "pharmacotherapy", "behavioral therapy", "supportive therapy", "dialysis". Distinct from MedicalProcedure, which is a broader category including diagnostic procedures.

candidates.label: MedicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a process of care, invasive or non-invasive, used for diagnostic, therapeutic, preventive, or palliative purposes. Also called medical intervention, clinical procedure, healthcare process. Examples: "surgery", "biopsy", "vaccination", "physical therapy".

candidates.label: DiagnosticProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure primarily performed to identify or confirm a disease or condition, rather than to treat it. Also called Medical test, diagnostic test, screening procedure, examination. Examples: MRI scan, blood test, biopsy, X-ray, colonoscopy. Distinct from TherapeuticProcedure, which is performed for treatment purposes.

types.embedding_query_text: InformationType: A category or classification of information based on its nature or characteristics. Also called data type, information category. Examples: misinformation.

chosen_type.label: InformationType
chosen_type.definition: A classification of data or knowledge, often referring to its nature or source.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type represents a general 'InformationType' like 'misinformation'; Intangible is a suitable parent.

candidates.label: DataType
candidates.comment: DataType is a fundamental classification for the kind of values that can be stored or manipulated, such as numbers, text, or booleans. Also called primitive type, data format, value type. Examples: Integer, String, Boolean, Float, Date.

candidates.label: BusinessEntityType
candidates.comment: A BusinessEntityType is an Enumeration representing the legal form, size, main line of business, or position in the value chain of an organization or business person. Also called legal entity type, company structure, business classification. Examples: Corporation, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Non-profit Organization.

candidates.label: MapCategoryType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".

candidates.label: CategoryCode
candidates.comment: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.

candidates.label: PurchaseType
candidates.comment: PurchaseType is an Enumeration listing different types of purchases for an item. Also called buying type, acquisition method. Examples: outright purchase, subscription, rental, lease.

types.embedding_query_text: Role: The function assumed or part played by a person or thing in a particular situation. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: trusted messenger.

chosen_type.label: Role
chosen_type.justification: 'Trusted messenger' describes a function or part played by a person, which is the definition of schema.org/Role.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: LinkRole
candidates.comment: A LinkRole is an intangible role representing a Web link, allowing for the specification of link relationships and other HTML link element details outside of HTML. Also called URL role, hyperlink descriptor, web link attribute. Examples: a link with 'linkRelationship' 'amphtml', a canonical URL link, a link to a related resource.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

types.embedding_query_text: Group: A number of people or things that are located, gathered, or classed together. Also called assembly, collection, body, team. Examples: committee of people.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: A 'committee of people' is a structured group with a particular purpose, which aligns with the definition of schema.org/Organization.

candidates.label: Collection
candidates.comment: A grouping of various items, which can include creative works or products. Also called assortment, compilation, set, aggregate. Examples: A collection of rare books, a stamp collection, a music album, a product catalog.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: DanceGroup
candidates.comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

types.embedding_query_text: Experience: Practical contact with and observation of facts or events. Also called expertise, knowledge, skill, background. Examples: decades of expertise.

chosen_type.label: Experience
chosen_type.definition: Practical contact with and observation of facts or events, leading to knowledge or skill.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent the abstract concept of 'Experience' or 'expertise'; Intangible is a suitable parent.

candidates.label: OccupationalExperienceRequirements
candidates.comment: OccupationalExperienceRequirements is an intangible entity indicating employment-related experience requirements. Also called job experience, work experience criteria, professional background. Examples: '5 years of experience in software development', 'entry-level position', 'management experience required'. Distinct from EducationalOccupationalCredential, which specifies formal qualifications.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: Observation
candidates.comment: An Observation is an intangible entity used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time, often quantitative. Also called measurement, data point, recorded value. Examples: a temperature reading, a stock price at a specific time, a survey response. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which is a specific type of observation with a numerical value and unit.

candidates.label: CourseInstance
candidates.comment: A CourseInstance is a specific offering of an educational course, distinguished by its particular time, location, medium, or target student group. Also called course section, class session, course offering, specific class. Examples: "Fall 2023 Introduction to Python (Online)," "Spring 2024 Art History 101 (Campus A, Section B)," "Summer Intensive Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from Course, which is the general description of the educational content.

types.embedding_query_text: HealthCondition: The state of a person's health, often referring to a specific medical status. Also called health status, medical state, well-being. Examples: Maternal Health.

chosen_type.label: MedicalCondition
chosen_type.justification: 'Maternal Health' refers to the state of health related to mothers, encompassing various medical conditions, fitting schema.org/MedicalCondition.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: MedicalConditionStage
candidates.comment: A medical intangible representing a specific stage of a medical condition. Also called disease stage, condition phase, severity level. Examples: "Stage IIIa cancer", "early-stage Alzheimer's", "acute phase of an infection".

candidates.label: HealthTopicContent
candidates.comment: HealthTopicContent is web content about a specific aspect of a health topic, such as a medical condition, its symptoms, or treatments. Also called medical web content, health information article, wellness resource. Examples: an article explaining diabetes symptoms, a webpage detailing cancer treatments, a video on heart disease prevention.

candidates.label: MedicalSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical sign or symptom that is a subjective complaint sensed and expressed by the patient. Also called subjective symptom, patient complaint, reported feeling. Examples: "stomachache", "lower-back pain", "fatigue", "headache", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalSign, which is an objective finding.

types.embedding_query_text: AbstractConcept: An idea or concept that is not concrete or tangible. Also called abstract idea, theoretical construct, notion. Examples: Quality, Strength.

chosen_type.label: Intangible
chosen_type.justification: 'Quality' and 'Strength' are abstract concepts that lack physical form, directly matching the definition of schema.org/Intangible.

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

candidates.label: ArchiveComponent
candidates.comment: An ArchiveComponent is an intangible CreativeWork representing any content within an archive, whether an individual item or a collection, described by specific archival properties. Also called archival item, archival record, archive content, collection item. Examples: a historical letter, a collection of photographs, a government document series, a digital archive file.

candidates.label: Intangible
candidates.comment: Intangible is a utility class serving as an umbrella for things that lack physical form, such as quantities, structured values, and concepts. Also called abstract entity, non-physical item, conceptual object. Examples: a number, a permit, a service, a list. Distinct from Thing, which is the root of all types, and CreativeWork, which is a specific type of intangible.

candidates.label: WebContent
candidates.comment: A general type representing any content accessible via the web, including web pages, websites, and their elements. Also called web content item, online content, digital web asset. Examples: a blog post, an entire website, an image embedded on a page.

candidates.label: DefinedTermSet
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a collection of formally defined terms, such as a glossary, dictionary, or classification scheme. Also called Glossary, vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, enumeration. Examples: The Dewey Decimal Classification system, a medical dictionary, a list of product categories, a set of industry standards. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a single entry within such a set.
